previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and chronic obstructive lung disease, was admitted with worsening shortness of breath, hypoxia, and chills following a suspected aspiration event. She had recently completed treatment for pneumonia and a UTI. Initial management in the MICU included broad-spectrum antibiotics due to concern for hospital-acquired pneumonia. Her condition improved with treatment, oxygen requirements returned to baseline, and she remained afebrile. Sputum culture identified MRSA, leading to de-escalation of antibiotics to vancomycin monotherapy. She was discharged home with a plan for six additional days of IV vancomycin via home health, stable respiratory status, and follow-up arranged with her primary care and pulmonary providers.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Evaluate for pneumonia in patient with recurrent pneumonias,
presenting with shortness of breath and low oxygen saturation, with a history
of T1-T2 paraplegia.

COMPARISON:  Multiple chest radiographs from ___ dating back to
___.

PORTABLE AP RADIOGRAPH OF THE CHEST:  There is new heterogeneous opacification
of the right lung base superimposed upon chronic atelectasis and fibrosis of
the same area.  The left hemidiaphragmatic contour is also obscured, although
this region of the radiograph is underpenetrated.  The upper lung fields are
clear.  There is stable severe cardiomegaly.  A right PICC terminates at the
cavoatrial junction.  There is no pneumothorax.  The left costophrenic angle
is not well visualized and a small effusion cannot be excluded.  Again noted
is dextroscoliosis of the thoracic spine as well as stable ribcage deformity.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Right middle and possibly lower lobe consolidation consistent with
pneumonia.
2.  Pneumonia involving the left lower lobe cannot be entirely excluded.
2.  Stable severe cardiomegaly with a right-sided predominance.

INDICATION:  ___ female with multifocal pneumonia.  Patient is T1-T2
paraplegic with history of recurrent pneumonias.

COMPARISON:  Multiple chest radiographs dating back to ___ and
CTA of the chest ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable upright chest AP radiograph.

FINDINGS: Lung volumes are low. Left lower lobe consolidation could be
pneumonia or atelectasis.  Dense consolidation in the right middle lobe may
also involve the right lower lobe, most likely represents pneumonia. Severe
cardiomegaly is stable. No pleural effusion is identified on this study. 
There is no pneumothorax.  The left costophrenic angle is not well visualized
and small effusions cannot be excluded.  There is stable ribcage deformity.
Upper thoracic dextroscoliosis is stable.  A right PICC line is seen in
appropriate position terminating within the low SVC. 

IMPRESSION:  Right middle and possibly lower lobe consolidation consistent
with pneumonia.  Stable severe cardiomegaly.
